newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE GAINS REVENGE AGAINST TORRANCE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE GAINS REVENGE AGAINST TORRANCE.

text.p: European number one Colin Montgomerie gained revenge over Scottish compatriot Sam Torrance to book a place in the final of the Andersen Consulting world championship regional competition on Tuesday.
Montgomerie, who lost to Torrance in the European final last year, produced a superb display to beat his rival six and four. He was meeting Italy's Costantino Rocca in the final later on Tuesday.
Rocca overcame Northern Ireland's Darren Clarke at the 19th in a far closer second semifinal to make his bid for the $200,000 regional final first prize.
In the first match, Montgomerie found his putting touch after saying on Monday that his form on the greens was at an all-time low.

He holed a 30-footer at the fourth to level with Torrance and an 18-foot putt for eagle-three on the long fifth to go ahead for the first time. He then sank from a similar distance on the par-four 13th to put himself five up with five to play.
Torrance ran an approach putt well past the hole on the short 14th and conceded the match.
In a desperate bid to resolve his putting problems, Montgomerie contacted his putter suppliers, whose factory is only a few miles from his home near the Buckinghamshire course.
"On the way home last night I telephoned Callaway and asked them to send round three putters," Montgomerie said.
"I chose one after a putting session on my carpet and left at 5.30 a.m. today to putt for an hour with it at the course before anybody arrived.
"I think my hard work's beginning to pay off. I've never worked so hard on one aspect of my game before."
In the second semifinal, Clarke won the first two holes and went three up after five but Rocca was back on level terms when the Irishman bogeyed the 14th.
Both missed chances from around five feet to win on the 18th before Rocca birdied with a 12-foot putt at the 19th.
The winner of the final will play three other regional champions from around the world in Arizona next January.
